## Single-case labelled values were reaching the output

`PGPASSWORD=tigertigertiger` and its shape were emitted verbatim. `looksLikeACredentialValue`
required a digit, or mixed case, or punctuation at twenty characters, and its own comment
noted that every leak-corpus entry qualifies on a digit or mixed case. That was true, and it
is why the gap survived: the corpus had no all-lowercase secret, so nothing measured the rule
against the shape it rejects.

A solid run of twelve or more letters, no digit and no punctuation, after `=` or `:` and a
credential-shaped name, is now a credential. Whitespace-separated values are unchanged.

Pure letters is the load-bearing restriction. The first attempt allowed any non-space run and
the benign corpus rejected it immediately with `key.anthropic`, `projects_json` and
`release-upload-key`. Identifiers carry `.`, `_` and `-`; passwords do not.

124 tests, benign corpus 0 of 64 mangled, leak corpus 0 survivors.
